utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom. We are still in the stage of examination-in-chief of this witness. Good afternoon to you as well. And, Mr. Vanderpuye, I suppose you have additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon to you, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Frease.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could have P125 back in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could repeat the number for the record. It was not recorded yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: P125, I believe. All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, I believe we left off with this document yesterday.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And we were going -- well, we had gone through the time that it was issued, which is indicated as 1400, to whom it was issued, and you indicated among the recipients of this document, or intended recipients of this document, was the commander of the Military Police Battalion of the 65th Regiment, and that was the military police of the 65th Regiment. And you've indicated that that was Zoran Malinic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it discusses a thousand members of the former 28th Division of the so-called BiH Army in the area of Dusanovo/Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, were you able to relate this particular document to any other intercepts, other than the two that we discussed yesterday?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Can I have P411B in e-court, please. All right. We'll need to go, as you can see -- well, it's not very well, but you can see, on this document, it is a print-out. We're not broadcasting it, are we? It's a print-out from the northern facility, and it's dated 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you see that and make that out?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could go, please, to the third page of this document in the B/C/S. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And on the third page, hopefully, you'll be able to see a part of one conversation and two other conversations. One begins at 1400 hours. It's between X and Y at 394. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And is that one of the conversations we discussed yesterday?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I just want to ask you, briefly, before we move on to the next conversation: Were you able to connect the extension 394 to any particular location?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not absolutely certain, so I'd rather not say.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Were you able to connect any other extensions, telephone numbers, in the intercepts that you reviewed to any particular person or location?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: 155 stands out.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what do you recognise that to be or what did you learn that that corresponded to?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That that corresponded to General Miletic's extension. It was actually, I believe, General Milovanovic's, but General Milovanovic had been away for a few months, and so Miletic was picking up on 155 most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'll come back to that in just a moment. But if we could page down, go down the page on this particular document, all the way down we'll see an intercept at 1405.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, this particular intercept is captured on the frequency 254.300, which is the same as the one immediately preceding it, and it indicates: "Direction, Pravac," "Y" and "I," "South-east." Do you recognise this intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we could have -- I hope we have an English translation of this one. If we could show both of them, that would be helpful at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In this particular intercept, were you able to relate this to the telegram that we just saw at P125?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this conversation mentions -- X mentions that he is going to be sending an urgent telegram.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the time of this one is at 1405?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you compare it or did you consider that in relation to the 1400 hours, which is indicated as the time on P125?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the order?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you consider that in terms of determining the authenticity of this intercept and also of the order itself?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye is trying to prove that two documents were identical, the one he showed first in the courtroom, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There's no -- perhaps I'm on the wrong channel. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This witness is being used to prove that the document of the 13th, at 1405, is identical to the document recorded at 1405 hours at the other end of the theatre. I don't think it is possible. In one case, we have an electronic record, and in the other, we have a typewritten text, and I don't see the correlation between the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I think, is able to deal with that. On the other hand, this is a typical remark or question. You could deal with that in cross-examination, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, there's a reference in this particular intercept to the football pitch, and --

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: There's a reference to, also, a telegram?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And a reference to -- well, there's a clear indication of the time. And you can see, from the original print-out on the right, that this document immediately follows the intercept which discusses a thousand prisoners at the football stadium?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says "more than a thousand."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you consider the relationship of this intercept at 1405 to the intercept at 1400, its subject matter, in relation to P125, which is the order that we discussed?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And as a result of having considered those factors, were you able to determine whether or not the intercepts were authentic and reliable and accurate?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a factor. Certainly, they are mutually corroborating.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you P2960.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think this number is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, it's 65 ter 2960. It's P842. Thank you, Ms. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, do you recognise this particular intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recognise what it's talking about, what the subject matter is?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a conversation between two unknown participants. They're talking about extension 394 being down at Kasaba, and then where Malinic's unit is, Malinic being Zoran Malinic, the head of the military police unit of the 65th Protection Regiment. And X says: "They said that there are 1500 gathered at the stadium." And that: "There were 1500 at the stadium in Kasaba."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you consider this particular intercept in the context of the other intercepts and the order we've just looked at?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does it confirm or corroborate the information that's contained, well, in all of those documents?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, they all relate to one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to show you another document. Just bear with me one moment. I'll give you the P number for it. Thanks. It's P774.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Ms. Frease?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it briefly in the last couple of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know what its origin is or what it purports to be?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know what its origin is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the extensions or telephone numbers of persons that are indicated in this document?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the locations that are indicated in this document?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. So let's start with this, for example, at Panorama. Do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the General Staff headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And where is that located?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Han Pijesak, Crni Vrh.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can I ask you: In this particular document, do you see, well, what's written here is "Lokal"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's an extension.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And if we go down this document, you can see these numbers that correspond to various names and locations.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we go down to "Panorama," you can see, for example, "General Gvero, Milan"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it's associated with extension 154?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if you go further down, you can see "Extension 155"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that's associated with, it says, "Puk Miletic"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I guess before a promotion. "Pukovnik" is the -- would be the short version for "Colonel" Miletic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And then you see it says "Oficir Pandzic"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it also says "Panorama"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we go a little bit further down, we can see General Gvero, it says "Cabinet for information." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that's associated with extension 157?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And further down, you can see "Extension 168"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you can see that's associated with a General Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it says "Puk Beara, Ljubo"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And then it says "Sekretar Zeljo"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are you familiar with these individuals, in terms of your analysis of the intercept materials? These names, I should say.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And to the right on that particular column, you can see it says "Glavni Stab." Can you tell us what that means?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: "General Staff," "Main Staff."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what about at 154? You can also see "General Gvero, Milan" -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If we can go to the next page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we go to this page, you can see other locations, such as "Bedem"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that name?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to look at the reference guide, but I think it's the Sarajevo -- it looks from here like it's the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And are you familiar with the code-names that are used in this document, generally?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally, sure. I mean, "Panorama" being the main one, certainly, on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of this extension 155, were you able to verify that extension with any other information that you came across while you were examining the intercept materials?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot cite one now, but I believe that there are intercepts that mention 155 and then associate names with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Very well, okay. I'd like to take you to a totally different area, and I'd like to show you an intercept --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you leave this topic, Judge Mindua has a question related to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Prosecutor. Actually, it's not a question, but a clarification. Likewise, Ms. Frease, we still don't know the origin of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: The origin of this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: -- we don't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I can tell you it, but I think the witness hasn't answered the question so I'll leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And we could see the first page, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is, as far as I know, the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At least the second. Now the first. Okay. The witness could perhaps help us to understand the origin of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What kind of document is it, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a document that came from ... all right. This is -- well, as far as the MIF is indicating, Mr. President, it indicates it was a document that was forwarded -- or seized by, I should say, the Bosnia and Herzegovina Intelligence and Security Agency, and it was also furnished to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2004, 6 July 2004. And it came together with other radio surveillance information, including some documents on a CD, which included documents totalling some 6.000 pages or so. But it was seized and turned over to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We see that there's no headline, no date, no signature. We can't see, from the document itself, the origin and who compiled this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand that. I'm not proposing to tender it through this witness, since she hasn't laid the foundation for it, and that's the reason why I said if she's not familiar with it, I'll leave it at that and I'll move on to a different area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. This is, indeed, a very good procedure. But I would like to ask the witness: How do you know that the extension number 155 is related to a specific person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Through years of work on the intercepts, some things stay in one's mind, and so through -- through just analysis. I can't point to a specific, you know, moment that I remember knowing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I want to take you to a different area altogether, Ms. Frease, and that has to do with some other intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have 65 ter 3497. It's a 22nd July intercept, and I think it's P773. Now, let's see which one we can get up here. Is it possible -- do we have P773 -- okay. It should be ERN 0080-1157.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, the Chamber learned that you want to use several documents related to this intercept, but there's only one offered to the Chamber yet under this number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, you're right. What we proposed to do was -- we have this -- actually, this is rather convenient. We have this print-out of the intercept. There is also an electronic version of the intercept which is more legible, and a handwritten version of the intercept which I think is also helpful, which we would like to use. We would like -- we would like to be able to show the Court this. They are substantively -- the electronic version and this photocopy are substantively identical, but this is actually a convenient moment because perhaps Ms. Frease can -- this coincides with Ms. Frease's testimony about the materials that the Office of the Prosecutor received initially. These are the photocopies that had some problems, in terms of legibility. So perhaps I'll ask her to comment on this, that we have it on the screen already. But I would like to ask your permission, the permission of the Chamber, to show her also the electronic version of this intercept and the handwritten version of the intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think there will be no problem. But first of all, you should move for adding these documents to the list of documents, because originally you only -- the Prosecution only asked for admission of one document, and it was given the P number 773, only one of them. But this is quite exceptional, because in other cases we have the numbers A, B, C, different versions of the same intercept, transcript and translation, so that we should, for the sake of the record, be very clear to which document you are referring.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise. I only realised -- and it is my fault. I only realised that this was a document that was loaded into e-court, as opposed to the electronic version and the handwritten version, which is what we try to do in most instances. I don't know whether or not the Registry has had a chance to designate the electronic version so that it can be used in e-court. We have. So if I may, with the Court's permission, I'd like to -- all right. I'd like move to have this document, which is P773, changed to P773A, and then to add P773B and C as the handwritten and the print-out, respectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The last one is a new print-out, because the first one --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- is an old print-out, if I understand that correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's right. This is a hard copy of -- it's a photocopy of something that was printed out long ago, and what I propose to add is -- yes, it's a new print-out from the electronic data that the witness has testified that the Office of the Prosecutor received subsequent to these hard-copy print-outs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is wrong with the first print-out?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The first print-out doesn't contain pertinent information relating to this intercept, such as the date, and I think that's particularly important in this instance. The date can be found on the first page of the report which contains this intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't understand that. The old print-out doesn't contain a date?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The old print-out does not contain the date on this -- that's right. On this page, it doesn't contain the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But it was a photocopy of the original or a print-out of the original transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. It's a photocopy of the original 500-and-some-odd pages of photocopied material that was provided to the Office of the Prosecutor back in 1998, I think it was, or thereabouts. March of 1998. Subsequently, as the witness has mentioned, the Prosecutor's Office received electronic -- that is, data disks, electronic versions of this material, and what we have -- what I'm proposing to add is the print-out from that material, which is substantively identical to this, in terms of the content of the intercept, but clearly it's not something that was compiled. It's something that's printed directly from the disk. So it contains the entire report for the day which contains this intercepted communication, among others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It would be helpful to elaborate with this witness and to show all these documents so that we can compare them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, do you have any problems by replacing one intercept by -- or adding three documents to one already-listed document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'd like to greet everyone, and may there be peace in this house. Let us conclude this exercise in keeping with God's will and not my own. It doesn't matter to me what the OTP is going to do, because all of these documents were copied and never used. The more we have of such material, the easier it will be for me to prove my assertions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In that case, the Registry will give the relevant numbers to the 65 ter numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. 65 ter 3497, previously marked as P773, is now marked as P773A. 65 ter 3497B is now marked as P773B. 65 ter 3497C is now marked as P773C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please carry on, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, and I do apologise for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First, Ms. Frease, can you comment on this particular document that you see in front of you? Can you tell us a little bit about it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the original documents. I can tell from the ERN number, which starts 0072. This was among the 550 pages that we first received in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, were these -- well, were these -- you've testified these were received in hard copy, or were they received electronically back in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us a little bit about that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And as a result of that, when these documents were translated, was that reflected in the translation?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How so?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As missing text, usually, though at times it also might not have been clear that the text was missing, so the intercept would just end.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. What I'd like to do, if I can, is to display --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, for the record, we have now P773A on the screen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Because it was not mentioned yet. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'd like to display alongside this exhibit P773C, which is the print-out. And we'll start with the first page, and we'll go through it up until we get to this intercept. All right, I think this is okay. We can start here. And we're not broadcasting it, are we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to raise the problem of legibility of this document. I was told that the witness can see it on her screen much better than the parties and the Chamber and the courtroom. Therefore, we can be sure that she is able to read it. For us it's really hardly legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It might be a good idea, Mr. President, if we can -- you know, we can blow it up section by section. I think we can maybe get through it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. At the top of this document, we can see it says "Armija Republike Bosne i Hercegovine"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: "2nd Corps," "Command of the 2nd Corps"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Then it has a location which indicates the northern site?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The strictly confidential number of 03/22795?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And then the date of "22/7/1995," 22nd of July?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what I'd like to do -- as you can see on this document, the first recorded communication, the first recorded intercept, is at 742 hours, 0742 hours?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now we can go to the next page, and we can go down.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You'll see the next -- well, the first recorded conversation on this page is at 902 hours and the one following at 0917 hours. You see that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And then if we go to the next page, all right. If we go down the page, you can see the conversation at 0928 hours?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I just point out one thing? That on that previous document that we saw, on the print-out, that 550 pages, that top line that was missing that I said you could kind of make out, but you couldn't really, you can see it if you look -- whoops, I touched the screen and everything got big. If you look two, four, six lines up in the previous conversation, so the one before 928, you'll see that line. "Hocete mi javiti." That was the line that was cut off on the print-out.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to do is if we could display them side by side so the Chamber can actually see exactly what the witness is talking about. Yes, it will be 773A and C, and it will be page 3 of 773C. I think we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We'll have to take the rubber band from the -- near the -- about a third of the way from the bottom, where you can see the words "Hocete mi javiti." Just about a third down. Down, down, that's correct. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, what you were referring to, Ms. Frease, was the very top of the document on the right, 773A?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that's the line that cannot be read?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you see that line on the document on the right, which is 773C?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you read it into the record?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Hocete mi javiti da znam da ssaljem auto jer gore mi trazze nemaju ni jedne." The "ni jedne" is on the line that is possible to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, this is a little bit problematic, because we can't understand. We hear the original version without translation, and it is not recorded because we have a record in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If you want to compare something, you should deal with the language in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. In this case, it's not a comparison in terms of what the substance of it is, because if it's possible, we can just blow up the words and we can see that the words are the same. And the meaning of it really is irrelevant. What we're concerned about and what I'd like to convey to the Trial Chamber is that the substances, that is, the language, the dots, the periods, the Xs, the Ys, are all identical in this material. So it really doesn't matter whether there's a translation. It's really more of a visual issue. I don't know if it's possible to blow it up in such a way that we can see the text so that you can follow just the words from one line to another, side by side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I understand very well what you are doing, but we must have it on the same level, the portions which relate to each other, so that we can compare it. And you should help the Usher to find the relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the relevant portion, for the purposes of the document on the left, is the first five lines of that document. It ends with "Zdravo," and the first line that you can see is "Ni jedne." That's the document on the left, which is now gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Including the top line, the black line we see there. It's important to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's right. It's gone now, but I'm sure it will be back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's the top five or six lines of the document on the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We need the document P773A on the left side of the screen, and especially the top of that page. Which page of that document is it, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It appears to be on the right page. It's just a few lines down. So if we can just go up on the document on the left, we'll be right there. There's the black line, and you have to go to the left now. All right, now it's back at the top of the page. If we can move it, fine. If we can't, then we can move the other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We need -- we need the black line and the following 10 lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's fine, that's fine. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And now on the same level, please, the same portion of the right document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Down a little bit, down. It should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please scroll up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The top line on the document should be the X that starts with the letters "H-o-c-h-e-t-e," "Hocete mi javiti," and that's just above the conversation at 928, six lines up in the conversation that starts at 928.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: More, more, more. No, the other way around, please. Yes. Further, further, further, further, further. Okay. If it's not possible, on technical reasons, please carry on. If the witness could indicate to which line you are referring, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure. So on the document on the left --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Actually, I have a great suggestion from Ms. Stewart, which would be for the witness to actually mark the lines, which I think she can do, and that will help everybody, I think. As you read them, you can mark them on both documents so that we can follow along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That is really a great recommendation for everybody in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right. So the first line is this one up here [marks], and it's the one where I said it's difficult to read, but you can see it [marks]. You can just make out enough of the letters, "Hocete mi javiti," and then it would be hard to say what that is, but when I look at the document on the right, I can see that it matches up with -- it's two letters, right, with "da," and it continues for the rest of the sentence. The next line down is "ni jedne," which is identical. Then we can see that line, so it's identical both of -- so I'll say line 2 here and line 2 there [marks]. And then the next line down just continues. This is an example of why it was important and helpful to receive the electronic print-outs from the ABiH and also from the MUP, because with the original documents that we received, there were passages that were missing just because of this photocopying issue. So we would be missing a couple of sentences and didn't know what they were. Once we received the electronic versions -- and also the note-books helped a lot in this, because through the note-books we could also see that the conversation continued. But the electronic versions mirror the information that we originally received in the 550 pages. And you can see, from the typeset and from the sentence -- the length of the sentences. In fact, if you go down two more lines, you can see the same mistake where there are two periods put after the same sentence. "Ajde molim vas.." should be just one period. There's no reason for two periods. It's a mistake, and the mistake is carried over also in the electronic version.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could you please mark that so that we can see exactly what you're talking about with the two periods on both documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]. Well, I think I wrote over them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And thank you for that explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could now just go to the bottom of the page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, we can't. We'll lose the markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I will tender these, then, into evidence at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: These documents, P773A and 773C, will be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And these are the original documents, and now the documents with the markings will be received as separate documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be received as Exhibit P864.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just wanted to briefly go down to the bottom of the page of 773A just to show the Trial Chamber what occurs there as well. You can see the black photocopy line which covers part of the text of that intercept as well, and this is -- I can ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was this something that was a consistent pattern in the photocopied material that the Office of the Prosecutor received, the 500-and-some-odd pages?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to actually get to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, may I ask you a question? Yesterday, we received these binders of different intercepts. Is this a document, P773, included in this binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, it's not. It's not included in that binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In that case, it would be very helpful if you could get a hard copy of these two different intercepts so that we have a better copy, so that we can read it, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll do that. I'll have it available to you after the break, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. And, of course, for the Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to do is just to get to the substance of this intercept. And to do that, I will need to go to P773B, which is the note-book, because I believe that's the one that has the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Frease, have you had an opportunity to review this particular intercept, which I think is responsive to a question that was put to you by Judge Nyambe yesterday, as concerns intercepts that were obtained in one location versus another location? Have you had a chance to review this particular one?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us, having reviewed this particular intercept, have you had an opportunity to compare it to any other materials?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to another intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And having -- do you know if these intercepts were obtained at the same sites or at different sites?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were obtained from different sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, have you had an opportunity to look at what the substance of this intercept is?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And have you compared that against the other intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of its substance, are they identical?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Why don't we have a look, then, at these intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If it's possible, I'd like to have -- I think I'm going to have to do -- I'm going to have to ask that the translation -- that we have this translation in the record, if it's possible to have P369B displayed side by side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But what about this document we have on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to -- well, I'd like to display them side by side, if it's possible. Otherwise, we'll do it sequentially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In English or IN B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: 369B, I believe is -- I think it's in English. I believe it's the English version or an English translation of another intercept which the witness has just talked about. All right, we'll have to go to the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, as you'll recall, Ms. Frease, the document on the left is from the northern facility, and the document on the right, as is indicated at the top of the screen, is from the southern facility.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the timing on the document from the southern site is 0931 hours?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The document on the left from the northern site is timed at 0928 hours?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's necessary to have the top of that page. Otherwise, we can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. And I'd like to, if it's possible, although I'm not sure if it is, to get these lined up somehow in e-court so that we can see the language that we have referring to both of these intercepts. I know it's a bit difficult, technically, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The left one is okay. The right one should be scrolled up. The other way around. It's not possible to do it further. Now we have it more or less on the same level.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. That looks pretty good. Thank you for -- thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And we can go line by line through this one. And the document on the left, which is the one at 0928 hours, starts off with: "Where is General Tolimir?" You can see on the right that this reads: "Is Tolimir around?"

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us, having looked at these documents and having looked at the original language, is that substantively the same? Was the language the same or was it different?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meaning of it is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay, all right. Do you know if the words that were used, written down by the operators, were the same or were they different?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We can take a look at that, then, as well in just a moment. But we continue down, and the second line says: "Here, right next to me." And that's on the document on the left. On the right, it's: "He's right next to me." The same question.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know if the language that was used in the originals was the same, or was it identical, or was it slightly different?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd have to look at both of them next to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And if we continue down the document, you can see, on the fourth line, it reads: "Just a moment." X says: "Just a moment." And on the document on the right, it reads: "One moment, please," which is followed by a comment, it says: "Popovic speaking. Hello." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And on the document on the left, after "Just a moment," there's a space, dot dot dot. What does that indicate to you?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they couldn't hear what T said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can I stop you for a moment. Mr. Tolimir. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. These two documents were not recorded at the same time, according to what is written here. One is at 9.28 and the other one is 9.31. This is a major time difference, since there is no time difference, actually, in the northern and the southern location. It's the same time zone. So I don't know exactly what this is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we had this problem already several times, and it's up to the Prosecution to elaborate on that and to find out what might be the reason for this difference. We see the difference. We have it on the screen and in the documents. Please carry on, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: As we continue down this document, and this is one of the reasons why we're comparing the substance of the document as opposed to the indicated time, which may reflect the time on a wall or somebody's watch, we're looking at the substance of the document, itself. As we continue down you can see, close to the bottom of the document on the left, which is the document that's timed at 928 hours, it says: "Sir, there's nothing yet about this cousin of mine. Popovic," it says, "did you manage to do find out anything?" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And then the document on the right says: "General, I don't have anything yet about that cousin of mine. Popovic, have you managed anything?"

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And following that, it reads on the document on the right: "There's nothing --" That's the document, for the sake of the record, that's at 0931 hours: "There's nothing." That's what T says. P says: "Nothing." T says: "Nothing." You can see that substantively the same, almost, on the document on the left?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can go further down on the document on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you go further down, it would be helpful if the witness could explain. Do you think about the reason -- what could be the reason of a different language of a quite similar conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We'd have to look at exactly what the language is, because sometimes it can be a matter of translation. Other times, if there is -- if there are slightly different words used, it can be how somebody's hearing it, depending on the location that they're at, and also how many times they've listened to it. If something sounds very similar and the meaning is "it's nothing," you could write it down -- you could, for example, invert the order of the words, "nema nista," "nista nema." So it could have to do with how many times the operator has listened to a particular conversation as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I don't know how much farther we can go down the page on -- okay. What I'd like to do is just to basically go through to the next page, I think it is, in the English translation on the left. It's at the end of the intercept. I can't see from this here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We need the next page on the left side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's fine. And if we can go to the next page in the document on the right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There's a problem with the translation, I can see on the document on the right. It's cut off, and so this would be a -- the conversation wasn't finished, whereas on the original document there were a couple more lines. So this is a classic example of, you know, sort of using documents that weren't complete and translations that weren't complete. I think if we looked at the original document --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We'll look at those in just a second.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just want to get this off the screen, and we can be done with it, and we can look at the original so we can actually compare the language that was used by the operators, themselves. But in this context, have you had an opportunity to review this -- you've reviewed all of these conversations?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in this context, is it the case that you have a conversation purportedly between General Tolimir and Popovic --

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, Witness -- I mean, Ms. Frease, are you able to go through this and identify where there are differences in the language? And if you could, maybe you could mark that.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. [Marks]. So that's missing, with the other small difference is the one on the left says: "Mogu li dobiti generala ..." "Can I get the general? utterances.text: Now, with respect to tab 1, were you able to compare this against other materials?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Contained within this folder?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, contained within the folder.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.text: May I ask a question? If I look at the B/C/S version, I only see the word "Micolai" with an M at the beginning. In the conversation, there's "General Micolai," and then with a question mark, "Nicolai."

utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has another question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: At page 48, lines 2 and 3, you are saying: "On the first intercept, the time is noted as 1517. On the second version," of the same intercept I assume, "it is noted as 1530, and that is reasonably proximate."
